props.title: Shoppers helped before and after checkout
props.lede: AI agents for brands and retailers that help shoppers pick the right size, close sales on WhatsApp, answer "where is my order" and run returns by your policy. They work on the storefront, OMS and couriers you already use.

intro.title: What does Exyconn build for retail and e-commerce?
intro.definition: is a group of agents that handle the questions and chores around every order: helping a shopper choose, recovering a cart on WhatsApp, answering where a parcel is, booking a return pickup and warning you before a bestseller runs out. Exyconn designs, builds and runs them on your storefront (Shopify, WooCommerce or your own), order management system and courier aggregator. Your support team handles the cases that need judgement.

benefits.title: Why retailers are doing this now

items.text: Shoppers already ask product questions on WhatsApp and Instagram, and expect a reply before they close the tab.
Order-status questions make up a large share of support tickets, and the answer is already sitting in the courier feed.
On cash-on-delivery orders, a quick confirmation message before dispatch can stop a parcel coming back unopened.
Returns and exchanges cost twice: the reverse shipment and the hours spent agreeing what happens next.
Stockouts on bestsellers and dead stock on slow lines both start as a forecast nobody had time to make.

props.label: The reality
props.title: Where a store's hours actually go
props.lede: Ask anyone running a D2C brand or a chain of stores. The list is long, and almost none of it is selling.

items.title: Pre-sale questions nobody answers in time
items.text: Size, fabric, "will it fit a 15-inch laptop". A shopper who doesn't get an answer within minutes buys the same thing on a marketplace.

items.title: Carts left at the payment page
items.text: Shoppers drop off over shipping charges, a failed UPI payment or a doubt about returns. A generic reminder email rarely brings them back.

items.title: "Where is my order?" all day
items.text: The agent opening the courier panel to copy a tracking status into a reply is the most common support task in the business.

items.title: Parcels coming back unopened
items.text: Wrong addresses, unreachable phones and second thoughts on COD orders turn into return-to-origin shipments you pay for both ways.

items.title: Returns handled by hand
items.text: Checking the window, asking for photos, deciding refund or exchange and booking reverse pickup takes several messages per return.

items.title: Reorders by instinct
items.text: Purchase decisions come from last month's sales sheet, so a festive spike or a viral post leaves you out of stock in the sizes that sell.

offerings.title: Six jobs AI takes off your team's plate

items.title: Product discovery assistant
items.text: Answers "what goes with this" and "which size" questions on your site and chat from your catalogue, size charts and reviews, and only recommends what is in stock.

items.title: WhatsApp commerce and cart recovery
items.text: Shows products and takes orders inside WhatsApp, follows up an abandoned cart with the shopper's actual question answered, and confirms COD orders before they ship.

items.title: Order tracking without a ticket
items.text: Reads live status from your OMS and courier aggregator, answers "where is my order" in the chat, and acts on failed-delivery reports by confirming the address or a new slot.

items.title: Returns and exchanges
items.text: Checks the order against your return window and policy, collects photos, offers an exchange size when it is in stock and books the reverse pickup. Exceptions go to your team.

items.title: Stock and demand forecasting
items.text: Projects demand by SKU and size from sales history, seasonality and upcoming campaigns, and drafts a reorder list for your buyer to approve.

items.title: Campaigns and reviews
items.text: Sends back-in-stock and new-drop messages to customers who opted in, asks for reviews after delivery and drafts replies to the critical ones for approval.

props.label: A day with it running
props.title: One day at a D2C apparel brand
props.lede: Follow a weekday in the run-up to a sale. Each moment lights the part of the store the agent is working on.

moments.title: Last night's COD orders confirmed
moments.text: Overnight COD orders get a WhatsApp check of address and intent. Two shoppers cancel, one fixes a wrong pin code, and only confirmed orders go to the warehouse.

moments.title: Tracking questions answered in the chat
moments.text: A run of "where is my order" messages gets live courier status in reply. One failed delivery is rescheduled for the evening with the customer's new landmark.

moments.title: A shopper finds the right fit
moments.text: A visitor asks which jeans suit a taller frame. The agent suggests two fits with the longer inseam, both in stock in her size, and she checks out.

moments.title: An exchange instead of a refund
moments.text: A customer says the shirt is tight. The agent confirms it is within the window, offers the next size up and books a pickup that brings the new one.

moments.title: Back in stock, to the right people
moments.text: The restocked olive kurta goes out only to customers who asked to be told. The agent also drafts a reply to a two-star review about late delivery.

moments.title: A reorder list before the sale
moments.text: Sell-through on the week's bestsellers is projected against the sale dates. The buyer wakes up to a reorder list by size, ready to approve or edit.

items.question: Does this replace our customer support team?
items.answer: No. It takes the routine questions such as order status, sizes and return windows, and passes damaged goods, payment disputes and unhappy customers to your team with the order and the conversation attached.

items.question: Which platforms can it connect to?
items.answer: Storefronts such as Shopify and WooCommerce, order management systems, courier aggregators, payment gateways and POS systems, as long as they have an API or a dependable export. We confirm exactly what your stack allows in the first week.

items.question: Can the agent issue refunds on its own?
items.answer: Only if you decide it should, within limits you set, for example store credit on items under a certain value. By default it collects the details and photos, and a person approves the refund.

items.question: Can customers write in Hindi or Hinglish?
items.answer: Yes. The agent replies in the language and mix the customer uses, including Hinglish and other Indian languages, and your catalogue and policies stay written once.

items.question: Is customer data handled properly?
items.answer: Order and contact data stay in your systems and an environment set up for your store, with role-based access and an audit log. Marketing messages go only to customers who opted in, and the setup follows India's DPDP Act 2023 and the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, or the GDPR for European customers.

items.question: What does it cost?
items.answer: It depends on order volume, channels and the systems we connect. Most stores start with order tracking and COD confirmation at a fixed price for the first phase. Tell us about your store and we'll quote it.
